name: Common frog
note: The common frog (docs 11, 12, 23). The recipe has two halves. The LOOK is body, bake and preview: what a later creature studio, and a player's look layer, may change. The LIFE is ecology, presence and find: needs, numbers, arrival and trust, which no look layer ever touches, so the core loop and catch-up stay the same. LOOK. body: the blended-SDF frog from Matt's pond tier 1 prototype (frog recipe v2), in real meters, body-local +z forward, origin on the ground under the body. prims are blended in order with a smooth minimum of radius k (m); rot is degrees about x, y, z; a capsule's r is [radius at a, radius at b]; a roundCone's scale stretches it about a. The throat sac is at rest (blend kRest). Eyes (Matt, 2026-10-19, after a photo of a frog's face): each eye is hooded from behind and above by a lid of skin (a piece with a part name, lid.l and lid.r, on the head bone; stiff, so its skin follows the head alone and the eye can sink under it). eyeLook: the eye looks out along axis (outward, up, forward), a wide horizontal pupil (half-widths across and up, shares of the radius) in a gold iris (albedo eyeRing) flecked darker (fleck, flecksPerM, fleckShare), beyond irisCos the ball (eye). displayScale: how much larger than life the frog is drawn (Matt, 2026-10-18: 1.5, so frogs read from a little way off on a big screen and show more detail on a phone); hops and tongue reach scale with it, comfort rings stay at real size. shape (S6b): named proportions the frog rig (src/world/creatures/rigs/frog.js) applies to the prims, 1 for the body as drawn here: torso length, width and height (the limbs and head move with the torso), head size (the eyes and throat follow), eye size, throat sac size, hind leg thickness. variation: each of variants seeded body variants nudges every proportion by up to this share and moves the blotches; every frog wears one variant, picked by its id, and is drawn up to sizeJitter larger or smaller. eyeGlint: the wet eyes, a smooth cornea (roughness) that shows a sharp point of sun or moon and the sky at a glancing view, strength times (physically lit; the skin that follows the eye bones). skin: how far (m) past the nearest piece a point of the skin still follows another piece's bone (smaller is a sharper fold at the joints). bake: the cell size (m) the body is meshed at by surface nets (the size preview), and lods: the levels of detail, each a cell size, used out to toM meters from the eye (the last beyond). motion (S6b): breath, the throat sac swelling by sac (share of its size) and the body by torso, hz times a second; blink, every everyS seconds (seeded), lasting s seconds: as a frog does, the eyes sink retractM into the head under their lids, flattened to squash of their height. S6b-2, from Matt's prototype export: frogs move on stepHz steps a second of real time (a hop takes as long at 4x), seeded per frog. hop: distM and heightM real meters (times displayScale, so hops scale with the drawn frog), lasting s seconds (longer for longer hops); the hind legs reach out to reach of their length in flight (two-bone IK) and the forelegs lift by lift (radians). squash: the body's landing spring, amount at most, stiffness k and damping d. call: while calling, a frog calls about perS times a second but waits if any frog started within gapS seconds, so the chorus runs around the pond; each call swells the throat sac to 1 + inflate times its size over pulseS seconds on a spring (k, d); a calling bout lasts boutS seconds. tongue: a flick lasting s seconds reaching reachM (times readability and displayScale) out of the mouth (body point), radiusM thick, albedo linear; while foraging, every everyS seconds. swim: a frog kick every kickS seconds at speedMps (times displayScale), then an eyes-up float of floatS seconds with eyesUpM of the head above the surface; only in water up to maxDepthM deep, where lilies do not grow. forage: a short hop every everyS seconds, then flicks tongue flicks. rest: a small shuffle every shuffleEveryS seconds. leashM: how far from its home on the bank a frog wanders. spacing: a hop never lands within hopBodies body lengths of another frog or its landing, and frogs closer than driftBodies drift apart at driftMps. pads (S6b-3): a frog whose home has lilies near spends about share of its outings on a lily pad, sitting or calling; only on a pad at least minRadiusM across its half (a grown pad), at seatShare of its radius out from the middle opposite the notch, its feet footM from the rim, clear by clearM of any pad that could swing over the seat; a pad within a hop it hops onto; one further out, up to seekM away, it swims to and climbs on from edgeM off its rim; one frog a pad, at most maxOn frogs on pads (the pad drawing dips those pads by dipM under the frog); a swimming frog ducks submergeM under a pad rather than through it, and floats only in open water. dayHide: by day (outside the activity hours, before calling) a frog sits tucked into cover within reachM of home, among the stems, and comes out to the edge at dusk: the cover score of a spot is the best of each kind there (reeds, rushes, iris as clumps or per-square cover, grass per square; weighted by cover), a spot counts from minScore, a meter farther off costs perM, searched on a stepM grid, on land or in water up to maxDepthM; it hops there until within atM, and looks again every againS seconds as cover grows; with no cover near, it rests at the edge. clumps: at night a frog sits outside this share of a reed or iris clump's radius, at its edge, never in its stems. moods: share of active time spent swimming; frogs at mood callFromMood or more call, from callAfterDuskH[0] to [1] hours after dusk. preview: the sizes the ?frogscale preview offers (times real), the camera distances (m) and pitches (degrees) of its views. LIFE. ecology (S6a, the hourly tick): dormancy names the window in recipes/world/seasons.json (asleep in the pond mud); activity: crepuscular, hours of the day it is out ([from, to), to past 24 wraps), for S6b. needs: five, each 0..1, mood = their weighted geometric mean (weights w sum to 1). water: distance to good water (still fresh water depthM deep, or a damp hollow), full within okM, none beyond maxM. food: the midge field (recipes/species/midge.json) summed over a square of radiusM around the spot, against perFrog times the group (shares of a full square meter of midges a frog needs). shelter: the best cover within radiusM, each plant weighted (cover), counting from 'from' and full at 'full' (grass alone is no shelter, so a bare grassy bank holds no frogs; long grass with other cover counts toward the web). quiet: what disturbs it by night and day (lanterns and paths, none in the slice, so 1 for now). company: frogs within reachM, full from n[0] to n[2] with n[1] ideal, a lone frog scores alone, a crowd past n[2] falls toward crowded. edge: a bank square beside a pond (still water of at least minPondM2 square meters; a spring's little pool is water, not a shore) is good edge when its score (mood at the ideal group size) is at least goodScore; the island holds one frog per metresPerFrog of good edge. scored: squares scored at all are land or shallows to shallowCm. arrival (times in game hours): the pond is right once the best edge scores rightScore and holds one frog, for rightHoldH hours in a row; a scout may come at dusk (duskOffsetH after sunset) once it has been right scoutAfterH hours and frogs are awake, with scoutChance each dusk and surely by the maxWaitDusks-th; after settleAfterH the scout stays if its mood is settleMood or more (and a second frog comes at the next dusk), else it moves on and none tries again for rescoutAfterH; then at dusk, if a day has passed since the last, mood is joinMood or more and there is room, another comes with joinChance; mood eases moodEase of the way to its target each hour; a frog whose mood stays under leaveMood for leaveAfterH hours, or one too many for the edge, moves on, at most one every leaveEveryH hours; the frogs are happy after happyHoldH hours at mean mood happyMood with happyMin or more. homeApartM: two frogs' homes at least this far apart. gift: what happy frogs give (the card is M2). presence (doc 23, S6b and S6c; rings in real meters): comfort ring ringM shrinking by ringTrustShrink x trust to ringMinM; a presence source (the camera's eye) inside the ring moving faster than calmSpeed m/s (times 1 + calmTrustGain x trust), or an edit within editReachM, startles a frog: it plops into the water, dives and swims about fleeM away from the source at fleeMps and floats eyes-up, wary for wariS seconds; frogs within hushReachM hush for hushS seconds; quiet watching (trust per minute in stretches of minS to capS within reachM), trust per feeding, the ceiling word and namingTrust. find: a frog is found (its page inks) when you tap the ground within tapM of it, plus tapPerM per meter the camera is away (a frog far off is small on screen), or watch it: keep it within lookM of the middle of your view, zoomed in to lookDistM or closer, for holdS seconds. The close-up limit (35 cm) lives in recipes/world/camera.json.
_reveal: Coming back in the reveal on return (S7c, src/world/creatures/reveal-return.js): return is how (plop: a ring on the water, for the few nearest the camera); growS is how long one takes to come in.
